items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier and Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-01-18
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah, like Joe Watkins. Yeah. Another fellow snags in Chicago.

ctx.x: See, he's got his position, his snags in the position. It's like a right-hand man be playing. But they say he got it to the left side. Now, if I was playing, I'd have a snag drum on this side, you see, with my right foot on the bass drum. But he's got it parallel to his left. But yet, no, I thought a left-hand drummer could have a snag drum like this.

Yeah, like Joe Watkins. Yeah. Another fellow snags in Chicago. Yeah. That's real left-hand drum playing like that. But he still don't play any of it. In that case, he's a right-handed drum player. But he didn't put it, see. Well, I understand.
So that makes him want to put the snare on.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: We had Joe Watkins on clarinet in sax. They used to play with the Si Morgan band too, Joe Watkins.

ctx.x: And the night we went on the Pelican to play it against the Pelican, the Silvertone Orchestra, with, that's when originally that split up from the original Tuxedo band. stuff

That's when he made up the band on the Pelican. Well I can give you some of the names of the men's. During that night when we had that band contest, well that didn't have, Black Happy on drum, and Bay Bay originally we had a boy by the name of Bat Brown on trumpet and Shot Madison. He got his picture in the other right. They was on the trumpet and some of the sax section. We had Joe Watkins on clarinet in sax. They used to play with the Si Morgan band too, Joe Watkins. Not Joe Watkins, the drummer.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: How come that Joe got back into the band and you left? ... So, Joe, King Goodall, try to help but, Earl Hines did that. So we left that morning and that's the same morning that happened to Joe Watkins, because he was living at the hangover club with George Lewis while we was in San Francisco.

ctx.x: How come that Joe got back into the band and you left?

Then, yeah, when I came to Los Angeles, that's why George Lewis told us that they was, they put a, give him a two weeks notice, but I'd play, just pay in advance. That's the union laws. Yeah. So, Joe, King Goodall, try to help but, Earl Hines did that. So we left that morning and that's the same morning that happened to Joe Watkins, because he was living at the hangover club with George Lewis while we was in San Francisco. So when we go down to Los Angeles playing down there, he, well a few days after we was in…
